questions.question: Draw or describe the classification tree for matter. Define a pure substance, a mixture, an element and a compound, and give two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Matter divides into pure substances and mixtures; pure substances divide into elements and compounds. Pure substance: only one kind of particle, fixed composition, sharp melting and boiling points (e.g. distilled water, sugar, copper). Mixture: two or more substances not chemically joined, in any proportion, separable by physical means (e.g. air, sea water, soil, tea). Element: one kind of atom, cannot be broken down chemically (e.g. oxygen, gold, carbon). Compound: two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio, broken down only by chemical means (e.g. water H2O, carbon dioxide CO2, sodium chloride NaCl).

questions.question: Explain what diatomic molecules are, list the seven diatomic elements with formulas, and explain why O2 is an element while H2O is a compound.
questions.expected_answer: A diatomic molecule is a molecule of two atoms chemically bonded. The seven diatomic elements: hydrogen H2, nitrogen N2, oxygen O2, fluorine F2, chlorine Cl2, bromine Br2, iodine I2. O2 contains only oxygen atoms, so it is still an element even though the atoms are joined; H2O contains two different kinds of atom, hydrogen and oxygen, chemically joined in a fixed 2:1 ratio, so it is a compound.

questions.question: Using sodium chloride and water as examples, explain how the properties of a compound differ from those of its elements. Count the atoms in CO2, NH3, C6H12O6 and 3CO2.
questions.expected_answer: Sodium is a soft reactive metal that reacts violently with water, chlorine a poisonous green gas, but sodium chloride is a stable white solid that is safe to eat. Hydrogen is flammable and oxygen supports burning, but water extinguishes fires. The new properties show a new substance has formed. CO2: 3 atoms (1 C, 2 O). NH3: 4 atoms (1 N, 3 H). C6H12O6: 6 + 12 + 6 = 24 atoms. 3CO2: three molecules, 3 C and 6 O, 9 atoms.
